prompt: A command-line tool usually runs once and exits before its code becomes hot. Which measurement best matches that use?

options.text: Include startup, interpretation and any compilation in time to the result
options.explanation: Correct. The user pays these costs before receiving the one result.

options.text: Measure only a fully warmed-up loop
options.explanation: A warmed-up loop measures a different workload and can hide the costs dominating this tool.
Compilation pauses are part of the observed use and should be included.

workedExample:
1. Identify the real workload: one invocation and one result.
2. Include the startup and runtime work required for that result.
3. Warmed-up throughput can still be useful separately, but it answers a different performance question.
